analysis:
No finding is supported by the visible diff; several contracts sit outside the supplied evidence.

ci.yml: the only change is one added test script at line 67 (test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py). The pinned actions, read-only permissions and gating are unchanged.

release-dev-branch.yml: only the path triggers changed (lines 71-72, 84-85). They add the cluster-runtime scripts, the Nemotron parity script and provider-test-shards.py. The trust model is unchanged: dev-branch pushes still get Developer ID signing, and the file's own comment says dev has no PR-review rule. Nothing new is introduced.

release-provider.yml:
1. qualify-sdk is split into a five-shard matrix, qualify-sdk-shard, plus an aggregate ubuntu job, qualify-sdk. The aggregate has no !cancelled() and needs the shard job. A shard failure therefore makes qualify-sdk skipped, not failed. Signing depends on qualify-sdk, and scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py also reads its result. The build-and-release 'if' condition and the resume logic are not in the supplied excerpt. If they treat 'skipped' as acceptable (for example result != 'failure'), a failed shard could let signing proceed without qualification. This needs checking against the real gate (A-017, T-054). The audit logic in scripts/provider-test-shards.py and the composite action that uploads the shard artifacts are also unseen. In particular, I could not confirm that a missing shard artifact fails the audit instead of passing on a subset.
2. A new step computes cluster_runtime facts by running the final signed app's own CLI and worker. It runs after signing and deletes the signing keychain first. It checks that the identity is gone, unsets r2_public_url and coordinator_url, and runs the app with an empty environment. The step is in the same job that holds the publication secrets, and the remainder of the job env is not shown. Whether anything secret-derived remains in the job-level env or GITHUB_ENV, and whether the later cleanup tolerates an already-deleted keychain, needs confirming. Executing built code here is an expansion of the build-and-release trust surface.
3. When CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true, the facts go to the coordinator in the registration payload. The coordinator is said to derive cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from them. These facts come from the build pipeline, not from an independently approved qualification (A-017, T-054). The coordinator-side acceptance and validation are platform-owned and not visible here. The default is off per environment through repository variables. The threat model likely needs an entry stating that this input is builder-attested.
4. The facts artifact is retained for 30 days. It is non-secret model and capability data, but its contents were not inspected.
